diffs.diff: minimum supply: part 3 V, datasheet reading 5 V
diffs.evidence: The second reading took the nominal '5V' label of M5Stack's PORT.A pin map (U001-C doc: 'M5Core(PORT A) GPIO22 GPIO21 5V GND'). M5Stack's ENV III schematic (envIII_sch_01) shows the Grove VCC pin (J1 pin 3) feeding an HT7533 LDO (VIN=VCC, VOUT=+3.3V) that powers both SHT30 (VDD=+3.3V) and QMP6988 (Vdd/Vddio=+3.3V), while the I2C pull-ups R1/R2 4.7 kOhm go to VCC itself, not to +3.3V. Sensirion SHT3x-DIS datasheet abs. max: 'Max Voltage on pins (pin 1 (SDA) ... pin 4 (SCL)) -0.3 to VDD+0.3 V', with VDD=3.3 V here, so a 5 V supply would pull SDA/SCL to 5 V, exceeding the SHT30 pin limit and 3.3 V MCU inputs. Running VCC at 3.0-3.6 V keeps the bus at 3.3 V logic and the HT7533 output (~VCC minus small dropout) stays inside SHT30 (2.15-5.5 V) and QMP6988 supply ranges. The model's 3.0 V minimum is the correct safe range for ESP32/Pico/Raspberry Pi use; the 5 V figure is the M5Stack host-port voltage, not a requirement of the unit.
